newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian funds should upgrade disclosures - SBC Warburg.
newsitem.headline: Indian funds should upgrade disclosures - SBC Warburg.

text.p: India's mutual fund industry must upgrade its reporting standards and bring them in line with international practices, investment firm SBC Warburg said on Wednesday.

"The most important thing is to (have) well-established reporting standards," Julie Hudson, Warburg's London-based director, Asian single currency funds research, told a seminar on the future of Indian fund management.
"The Indian industry will do well to emulate the U.S. and Thailand," Hudson said. "Data cleaning is the key to evaluating performance in India."
Thai mutual funds unfailingly communicate their NAVs (net asset values) to the stock exchanges each Friday and disclose their portfolios every quarter, she said.
Hudson said evaluating performance of Indian mutual funds was a difficult exercise as data were scarce and suspect.
A.P. Kurian, chairman of the Association of Mutual Funds of India (AMFI) said his organisation was working to institutionalise disclosure norms for Indian industry.
"We (AMFI) are going to be a clearing house. We will compile and disseminate (mutual fund disclosures)," Kurian said.
Participants at the seminar said the NAVs released by Indian funds -- income funds in particular -- were suspect as many debt market instruments in their portfolio were not traded.
Kurian said AMFI has asked Price Waterhouse to help design a system for valuation of unquoted shares in a fund's portfolio.
